title: Parallel Courses III
summary: Given an integer n representing courses labeled 1 to n, and a 2D array relations showing prerequisite courses, along with a time array indicating the months needed for each course.
statement: Given an integer n representing courses labeled 1 to n, and a 2D array relations showing prerequisite courses, along with a time array indicating the months needed for each course. Determine the minimum months required to complete all courses, starting any course when prerequisites are met and taking multiple courses concurrently if possible.
constraints: Courses are numbered 1 through n; relations is an acyclic prerequisite graph.
Any number of available courses may run concurrently, and time[i] is course i+1 duration.
Return the minimum months until every course is complete.
hints: With unlimited concurrency, completion time is the longest weighted prerequisite path.
Process courses topologically, propagating the maximum predecessor finish plus the next duration.
Initialize sources with own durations; relax finish[v]=max(finish[v],finish[u]+time[v]).
Topological order finalizes every predecessor before its dependents, and the maximum incoming path is exactly the earliest possible dependent start.
editorial: Topological order finalizes every predecessor before its dependents, and the maximum incoming path is exactly the earliest possible dependent start.

tests.explanation: Course three begins after the slower prerequisite at month three and finishes at month eight.
The longest prerequisite chain takes twelve months.
